newsitem.title: POLAND: MINORITY STAKES MAY DELAY POLISH NFI FLOATATION.
newsitem.headline: MINORITY STAKES MAY DELAY POLISH NFI FLOATATION.

text.p: The planned floatation of Poland's mass privatisation National Investment Funds (NFI) on the Warsaw bourse could be delayed by the consolidation of minority stakes of firms in the NFI scheme, the bourse's president said.
Wieslaw Rozlucki said NFI funds should first begin public trading on the bourse before minority stakes in the 514 firms in the mass privatisation programme were consolidated.
"I would like (NFI) funds to trade publically before consolidation of the minority stakes," Rozlucki told reporters.
Under the mass privatisation sheme 514 state-owned firms, worth more than $2 billion, are grouped under 15 NFI funds, which will later be traded on the Warsaw bourse.

A 33 percent stake of each firm in the scheme is owned by the fund under which it is grouped, some 25 percent is owned by the state treasury and a 1.9 percent stake is distributed to the other 14 funds.
The rest is owned by employees and set aside for reprivatisation claims.
Bourse officials said the planned consolidation of the small 1.9 percent stakes could delay NFI entry on the stock exchange, earmarked in the first quarter of 1997.
The head of NFI No. 6, Krzysztof Bialowski, also present, said that a consolidation deal between eight of the NFI 15 funds could be made in the next several days.
Under the scheme, 28 million adult Poles can, for a nominal fee, buy units which will later be exchanged for 15 shares, one in each of the programme's 15 funds.
